title: Tenstorrent
summary: Toronto AI-chip company pairing RISC-V CPUs with accelerators and licensing its designs.
bodyHtml:
Tenstorrent designs AI accelerators and RISC-V CPU cores, led by chip architect Jim Keller. It sells chips, systems and IP licences.

The strategy is to offer an open, licensable alternative to closed accelerator stacks, with a focus on inference and on customers who want to own part of the design.

Why it matters

  • RISC-V CPU IP
  • AI accelerators and systems
  • Open software stack

businessMeaning: The accelerator market rewards software ecosystems as much as silicon. Tenstorrent's licensing model is a way to reach customers without building a full cloud business.
investmentLens: Private; the thesis is architectural openness winning design slots, which would show up in foundry and packaging orders.
